(US Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit, 18 Mar 2025)

Thaler v  Perlmutter
(US Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit, 18 Mar 2025)
•                                                                       Facts:
          –                                                        Dr Thaler built an AI called the “Creativity Machine”
          –                                                       It made an image,  “A Recent  Entrance to Paradise”
          –                                                       He applied to register copyright, naming the  machine as the  only author
•                                                                       Issue:                        Can a machine be an “author    ”                under  US copyright law?
•                                                                       Ruling:
          –                                                       No –                           a work must be  created in the  first instance by a human being
          –                                                       The US Supreme  Court refused to hear his appeal (2 Mar 2026)
•                                                                       Lesson:                       In the US, no human author means no copyright                                                                                      (版权)

李某诉刘某(北京互联网法院,(2023)京0491民初11279号)
•                                                                       Facts:
          –                                                        Li made  an image  with Stable Diffusion
          –                                                       He chose the  prompts and adjusted the  settings, then posted it online
          –                                                        Liu used the  image  without permission and removed  Li ’s signature
•                                                                       Issue:                        Is an AI-generated image protected, and  who is the author?
•                                                                       Ruling:
          –                                                       Ye      s        –                          it is a work of art
          –                                                        Li, the  user, is the author: the  AI has no free will of its own
          –                                                        Liu infringed Li ’s copyright
•                                                                       Lesson:                       In China, a user    ’s prompts and choices can be enough.                                                                                       The  Chinese court
       looked at the user's prompts and parameter choices as creative input.

(US District Court, N.D. California, 23 Jun 2025)
full_extracted_page_text:
Bartz v  Anthropic
(US District Court, N.D. California, 23 Jun 2025)
•                                                                       Facts:
             –                                                       Anthropic downloaded millions of pirated books (illegitimate source)
             –                                                       It also bought                      print books and scanned them                                                                                                                        (legitimate source)
             –                                                       It kept a central library and trained its AI, Claude
•                                                                       Issue:                        Is each step “fair use”: (1) training, (2) scanning bought books,  (3) keeping
         pirated copies?
•                                                                       Ruling:
             –                                                        Training: fair use
             –                                                       Scanning books it bought: fair use
             –                                                       Pirated copies (盗版书)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               : not fair use at this stage –                          sent to trial
             –                                                        A class settlement   was finally approved on 20 Jul 2026
•                                                                       Lesson:                       How you obtain the data matters as much as how you use it

•                                                                       Lesson:                       Copying to build a direct competitor is hard to defend

•                                                                       Lesson:                        The  human  “backup” can  still carry the  criminal risk
